name: Philosophy
note: Mostly epistemology and ethics — how a claim earns the right to be believed, and what follows once it does.

name: Psychology
note: Reasoning and bias, particularly the ways a conclusion can feel obvious before the evidence has been read.

name: Self-improvement
note: Treated as a practical question rather than a motivational one: which habits actually hold up over months.

name: Technology
note: Building things well enough to understand them from the inside instead of only reading about them.

name: Indian politics
note: Institutions, incentives and how policy actually travels from announcement to implementation.

name: History
note: Long time horizons, and how the choice of a start date quietly shapes the conclusion.

name: Current affairs
note: Following events closely enough to notice how the first account differs from the fifth.

name: Public policy
note: Trade-offs rather than positions — what a policy costs, who bears it, and what it was measured against.

name: Data
note: Imperfect datasets in particular: missing years, changed definitions, and sources that disagree.

name: Cybersecurity
note: An interest I'm currently learning, not one I can claim skill in — fundamentals and defensive thinking.

name: Education and academic learning
note: How material is structured for learning, which is where the worksheet generator design came from.
